records.issue_text: Non-admin users can push 10 MB images through uploads_controller; SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb no longer bounds anything server-side except the downsize loop, and the 10.megabytes cap only applies to the API URL path, making the effective limit hard-coded rather than admin-controlled
records.rationale: The diff hard-codes a 10MB limit in the client (`maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024`) and in the API URL download path (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`) instead of using `SiteSetting.max_*_size_kb` / `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. records.issue_text: Downsize loop in uploads_controller resizes in place (tempfile.path as both source and destination) and never checks the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize, so a failed convert leaves a truncated/corrupt file that is passed to Upload.create_for as valid

Up to five synchronous ImageMagick convert invocations on a 10 MB image run inside the request cycle, blocking a worker for many seconds and creating a resource-exhaustion vector for any logged-in user
records.rationale: The diff adds a synchronous loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that can run up to 5 times (`attempt = 5` / `while attempt > 0`) calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)`. `OptimizedImage.convert_with` executes ImageMagick via backticks (external `convert` command) synchronously. This all happens inside the request cycle for any user upload, and the earlier change raises the client/server limit

records.issue_text: FileHelper.is_image?(filename) matches by extension, so non-images or SVGs with a .jpg name are passed to convert in place; allow_animation is gated on SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails (a thumbnail setting), so uploaded animated GIFs are flattened when that setting is off
The 413 alert in utilities.js reports a hard-coded 10240 KB regardless of the actual web-server body limit or site setting that triggered it, so the error message can state a wrong limit
records.rationale: In utilities.js, the 413 (entity too large) handler was changed from using `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hard-coded `10 * 1024` (10MB). This makes the alert always report 10240 KB regardless of the actual configured limit or upstream web-server body size limit that triggered the 413, so the error message can be incorrect.

records.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new behavior in `UploadsController#create_upload` (a retry loop that downsizes oversized images up to 5 times using `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)`), but the diff shows no accompanying test changes.
